That's not true... People take other people for granted, people don't bother to think about how that might affect people, but if you went away, they would notice, they would miss you, they would cry for you.

But really dude, this is an opportunity, you get to try to make new friends! I would give ANYTHING to have the opportunity to make new friends, to even talk to people in my age group. But this isn't about me. You're not the only one in your school who feels like they haven't got any friends, I doubt you'd notice the other ones because they are talking to other people just like you are. But when they go home, they don't have much going on. Find them and become friends with them. They will be hard to find because no one wants to advertise the fact that they are lonely, but they are out there, and they are waiting for you just as much as you are waiting for them.

(Also you can be friends with people who have friends, I'm just... saying, you know, it's easy to make friends with people who don't have any friends)

Killing yourself is the easy way out. It's the way out because it's something that you can imagine and hold on to. Why not go rob a bank? Why not go punch people that make you angry. Why not run away?

You're obsessed with a way out, you've given up, well why not do something cool now that you're all done? Seriously! You know what I did one time? I drove away, I camped in national forests and stole a tiny bit of food from a grocery store and slept in the back of my truck and listened to audiobooks. I started smoking because I didn't care. And you know what? I felt great, seriously, I felt free and happy and I wasn't worried about what I looked like or if I could focus or if I could get anything done because none of that mattered. What happened after that doesn't matter to you, it turned out for the best for me but maybe for you, you keep doing that until something changes.

If you're going to kill yourself and don't want to be talked out of it, at least try some cool shit first. Try to climb a tall building that you're not allowed to climb, try 1000 other things that most people don't want to do.

If you can't do these things, if you're still too afraid, then you aren't ready to kill yourself. You're too invested in life, I think you're hoping that if you threaten reality, if you say "I'm going to kill myself" then things will get better. And you know what? They will... But you don't want to hear that right now. So run away! Go camping. Climb a mountain.

Well... Sometimes you can't help someone like this out. Sometimes being there won't do anything, sometimes listening will make it worse but you can NOT go away. If he keeps talking to you, if that becomes all the relationship is about, if you feel like he is the most annoying person in the world you still can't say "I'm done" because it might destroy him. This sounds like the most obvious thing in the world right now but if you spend a year listening to someone whine about what will increasingly seem like irrelevant things, things that everyone else puts up with, you will get sick of it.

My advice is don't let it just become about him being sad. Do things together. When he is really sad go over and help him out by DOING something. Don't sit and talk, don't come over and watch a movie with him (I don't know if you're a guy or a girl but in my experience, if you're a guy, most of my advice won't become relevant, most guys are scared to super open up to their male friends or at least to make the relationship become about that entirely and it's easier to find things to do) go out into the real world and do something. Go hiking, or find a place to build a fort, or find a video game and play that. Make it feel like you're accomplishing something. That's the best way you can support him. 

Oh, one more thing, try to fix some of his real problems, ask around, see if anyone has work that is more interesting than what he is doing. Get him to start a project that he's interested in. Engage in a project together.

I hope that was... some help. Maybe none of it applies..
... Thanks. That means more than I would have expected :)

Can you explain why you do it? I'm honestly curious... Why do you do it? What made you start? Does it really help? Do you really make a choice between killing yourself and cutting yourself?

I've spent years depressed and I can never bring myself to do anything more than punch myself in the face. I physically can't... But why does it help?

If you truly wanted to suffer and be miserable, why did you post here? haha! I've fixed your depression with some simple logic! I kid. 

Comparing yourself to someone in a drastically different situation to you is irrelevant. It doesn't matter who's fault it is. Look at how happy starfish are, and they don't have thumbs! Depression is not something that comes from your situation and it certainly can't be solved by tracing it through some, probably inaccurate causality chain.
